title: DRIPR
subtitle: Product Design Concept
description:
The Quick Snapshot
Project Type: Self-Initiated Product & Packaging Design

Focus: Packaging aesthetics, label design, print materials, and promotional assets.

Industry: Wellness & Beverage.

The Vibe: Sharp, modern, and high-impact.

The Concept (The Product)
DRIPR isn’t just a drink; it’s an experience. The goal of this project was to design the physical "face" of the product—the label and the accompanying promotional materials.

In a competitive market, a product needs to do more than just sit on a shelf; it needs to signal its purpose instantly. I designed DRIPR to cut through the visual clutter of standard beverage aisles by using bold, clean typography and a confident, minimalist layout that tells the consumer exactly what they are getting at a glance.

The Approach
My process was driven by how a customer experiences the product:

Packaging & Label Design: I approached the label as a functional piece of art. The design uses aggressive, modern typography and a high-contrast palette to establish a distinct "shelf presence." Every element—from the hierarchy of the product information to the placement of the logo—was chosen to ensure the product feels premium and purposeful in the consumer’s hand.

Promotional Design: The supporting flyers were designed to act as an extension of the packaging. They share the same visual language, ensuring that whether a customer sees the bottle or a promotional poster, the "DRIPR" aesthetic remains unmistakable.

Holistic Cohesion: The most important part of this project was ensuring that the packaging and the marketing materials felt like one unified system. If the design on the bottle doesn't match the design on the ad, the message is lost.

Why It Works
This project succeeds because it relies on visual clarity. By stripping away unnecessary design noise, I let the product’s identity do the heavy lifting. The result is a clean, bold system that looks ready for retail, feels professional, and makes a strong impression the moment it’s picked up.

title: MIKITA
subtitle: Fine Jewelry Brand Identity & Concept
description:
Brand Identity Concept: MIKITA — Held in Elegance
The Quick Snapshot
Project Type: Self-Initiated Brand Identity Concept

Industry: Fine / Luxury Jewelry

Focus Areas: Logo design, color theory, brand voice, packaging mockups, and campaign art direction.

The Vibe: Intimate, poetic, calm, and quietly confident.

The Backstory (The Concept)
Every piece of jewelry carries a story, but I wanted to explore a brand that focuses on the feeling of wearing it rather than just the price tag. I set out to design a concept for a luxury jewelry brand called MIKITA, built around the philosophy of "holding what matters"—the idea that personal adornments act as anchors for our memories, emotions, and identity.

Because this was a self-initiated project, I didn't have a real client dictating the rules. Instead, I gave myself the brief to create a premium, high-end identity that felt warm and approachable, rather than stark, intimidating, or overly flashy.

The Visual Identity
1. The Logo & Mark

The Symbol: At the center of the circular badge is a hand-sketched open shell cradling a delicate pearl. The shell represents protection, intimacy, and natural beauty, while the pearl embodies timeless elegance.

The Layout: The circular stamp design gives it a classic, heritage feel. I created two primary variations—a soft dusty-rose version on an off-white base, and a rich, moody plum version for darker applications—ensuring versatility across different mediums.

2. Color Palette & Typography

The Palette: MIKITA’s palette balances moody depth with gentle warmth. It features:

Deep plum/charcoal (for grounding)

Dusty rose and soft mauve (for femininity and emotion)

Cream and muted gold (for luxury and softness)

The Type: I paired a graceful, high-contrast serif font with plenty of open breathing room. This allows the typography to feel sophisticated and editorial without shouting at the reader.

Brand Personality & Voice

To make sure the brand felt like a fully realized world, I mapped out its core pillars:

Keywords: Minimal, Timeless, Intimacy, Emotional Value, Elegance, and Soft Power.

Tone of Voice: Calm, confident, and slightly poetic. The golden rule for MIKITA’s copy is that it is never loud or salesy. It invites the customer in rather than pushing a product onto them.

Campaign & Packaging Applications
To show how the brand lives in the real world, I put together a few mockups and campaign drafts:

1. Art Direction & Campaign Visuals

The photography focuses on natural, soft lighting, delicate fabrics (like tulle and silk), and earthy elements like feathers and shells.

The posters feature the headline "Held in Elegance," cleanly integrating the logo and vertical text layouts to give it a high-end magazine or editorial feel.

2. Packaging Design

The unboxing experience is designed to feel like a gentle reveal.

The jewelry box is a clean, textured beige/cream with the MIKITA wordmark subtly embossed in gold, accompanied by a rich velvet pouch.

The shopping bag follows the same minimalist, tactile aesthetic, featuring premium twisted rope handles and clean, understated branding.

The Takeaway
MIKITA was a fantastic exercise in restraint. It proves that luxury doesn’t need loud neon colors, heavy drop shadows, or aggressive marketing to feel premium. By relying on soft textures, elegant typography, and a very human, emotional narrative, this concept successfully bridges the gap between high-end appeal and everyday accessibility.

It stands as a solid, evocative draft that immediately communicates to potential clients how their own brand stories can be brought to life with grace and clarity.
